searchText: This is not exactly a cap in the traditional sense of the word (I assume a cap meaning a maximum allowed). It is more like some are active, some are dormant, and there is switching between them after certain numbers of epochs The actual cap in the protocol is set to be a massive number interesting... curious what is the advantage of a hardcap over letting the market decide how much ETH to stake (knowing full well the return degrades w/ more validators)? in all scenarios (that I can think of) the end nodes running the beaconchain and a validator would have to track active and dormant validators (so still memory intensive)... so it would seem the economics degrade if more than 1MM validators show-up.. curious why the hard limit? Network resources to transport attestations, CPU resources to aggregate attestations. 🤔 curious, are those two items not set to also scale with time? e.g. will the technology outpace the possible constraint? It's more of a safety bound for resource consumption, which could be increased if the technology keeps up with the validator set growth. fair point..
